sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by ELISA-based quantification of c-myc-OR1740 in cell membrane nanovesicles; functional assay (e.g., ligand-induced signalling) NOT MEASURED in the cited study.
sites.rationale: The paper names no residue and no specific loop; the construct label 'c-myc-OR1740' follows the standard N-terminal fusion convention for GPCRs. OR3A1 has no signal peptide (topology begins extracellular at residue 1), so the N-terminus is directly extracellular (EC1, residues 1–28). The C-terminus (residues 296–315) is intracellular, leaving exactly one extracellular terminus; topology_derived therefore places the tag as a prepend before residue 1 (insert_after_residue = 0). The prepend site is 28 residues from TM1 (starts at residue 29), well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. PMID 26724468 reports a c-myc-tagged OR1740 (OR17-40/OR3A1) full-length receptor expressed in cells and quantified on the cell membrane surface via ELISA-based immunochemical detection in nanovesicles. The construct is named 'c-myc-OR1740', indicating an N-terminal fusion. No residue number or loop name is given.

sources.claim: The applicability of the method is demonstrated through the quantification of the c-myc-olfactory receptor (OR, c-myc-OR1740) in the cell membrane NVs. The reported method opens the possibility to develop well-characterized drug-screening platforms based on G-coupled proteins embedded on membranes.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is available. It reports surface display of a c-myc-tagged OR3A1 (OR1740) in a full-length, membrane-anchored context, qualifying as a valid insertion. However, no residue number and no loop name are given; the position is derived solely from the construct naming convention ('c-myc-OR1740' = N-terminal fusion) and the fact that OR3A1 has exactly one extracellular terminus (the N-terminus, EC1 residues 1–28; the C-terminus is intracellular). No internal loop sites (EC2 86–100, EC3 170–199, EC4 264–275) are supported by the ledger. Confidence is medium because the junction is topology-derived, not explicitly stated.

literature_other_positions.note: The C-terminus of OR3A1 (IC4, residues 296–315) is intracellular per topology landmarks; a tag here would not be surface-displayed and is not supported by L1.
